To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
necklace-like NiO- CuO heterogeneous composite hollow nanowires can be synthesized by annealing in air.
necklace-like NiO/CuO heterogeneous composite nanostructures were synthesized via annealing Ni/CCu superlattice nanorod arrays.
necklace-like NiO- CuO heterogeneous composite hollow nanowire was prepared by annealing Ni/ Cu superlattice nanorods in air.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of composite hollow nanostructures, and it may provide a new way for preparing other transition metal oxides based composite hollow nanostructures.
the formation of hollow structure and its control.

the preparation of transition metal oxide composite hollow nanostructures with controllable structures and morphology, which is of great significance in the development of novel materials and devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation mechanism of necklace-like NiO/CuO heterogeneous hollow nanostructure is the result of Kirkendal effect, high temperature oxidation and the diffusion of Ni and Cu elements.
the relative length of Ni and Cu in Ni/Cu nanowires and annealing temperature are the two main factors influencing the formation of the final structure.

the annealing process of Ni/Cu super-lattice nanowires could be divided into three stages: (1) the formation of Ni/Cu alloy nanowires, (2) the formation of core-shell structure and (3) the formation of hollow structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the annealed sample morphologies are determined by the relative diffusion amount of alloying elements, the oxidation of alloy and the annealing atmosphere.
the formation of composite hollow nanostructures is a result of Kirkendal effect driven oxidation of the alloy nanowires.

the annealing temperature is the key factor to determine whether the oxidation exists or not, and the diffusion rate of Cu to Ni determines whether the oxidation is in external sites or in both external and internal sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the formation of necklace-like NiO hollow nanotube and NiO-Cu _{2} O core-shell nanotube structures are both related to Kirkendal effect, but the oxidation process of NiO-Cu2O core-shell structure is more complicated than that of hollow structure.
the structure of NiO-Cu composite hollow nanostructure can be controlled by adjusting the length of Cu segments and annealing temperature.
we provide a new way for the fabrication of transition metal oxides hollow nanostructures and give a detailed formation mechanism of necklace-like NiO/CuO hollow nanostructures.
